title: Pixie Cut Styling Tutorial
metaDescription: How to style a pixie cut day to day, from the initial grow-out awkward stage to a finished textured look — the products and technique that keep it from looking flat.
toolsNeeded: Fingers or a small paddle brush

steps.name: Apply product to damp hair
steps.text: Rub a pea-sized amount of texturizing paste between the palms and work it through damp hair from root to tip, focusing on the top and fringe area.

steps.name: Dry with lift
steps.text: Blow-dry using fingers to lift the roots upward and forward rather than flattening them with a brush, which is what gives a pixie its shape.

steps.name: Piece out the top
steps.text: Once dry, use fingertips with a small amount of extra paste to pull individual pieces of the top section into place for texture.

steps.name: Define the sides
steps.text: Smooth the shorter sides and back down with a small comb or the palm of the hand for contrast against the textured top.

steps.name: Set lightly
steps.text: Mist with a light-hold spray only over the top texture, keeping the sides untouched so they stay soft rather than stiff.

tips.question: Why does a pixie cut go flat within a couple of hours?
tips.answer: Skipping the finger-drying-with-lift step is usually the reason — pixies rely almost entirely on how the roots are dried, since there's very little length or weight to build shape from otherwise.

tips.question: How much product is actually needed for a pixie?
tips.answer: Far less than most people use — a pea-sized amount of paste is enough for most pixie lengths, and too much product weighs the short top section down instead of adding texture.

tips.question: What's the best way to manage a pixie during grow-out?
tips.answer: Regular trims every 4-6 weeks on just the neckline and sides keep the shape clean while the top grows longer, which is usually the part people want to grow out first.

storyIntro: A pixie cut lives or dies on the styling, not the cut itself — the same haircut can look sharp and intentional or completely flat depending entirely on how the roots are dried.
The finger-drying technique that lifts hair up and away from the scalp while it dries is what most pixie tutorials skip, and it's the single biggest difference between a styled pixie and a limp one.
storyNote: Work product through hair while it's still damp, not after it's already dry — paste applied to dry pixie hair tends to sit on top in clumps rather than distributing evenly through the shorter strands.
